papers.title: Droplet digital PCR-based nucleic acid amplification test for improved molecular and clinical diagnosis of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome patients
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is caused by SFTS virus (SFTSV) and is characterized by high mortality and non-specific clinical manifestations, which make early and accurate molecular diagnosis essential. This study aims to investigate whether reverse transcription droplet digital PCR (RT-ddPCR) provides improved diagnosis of SFTS compared to existing molecular diagnostic platforms. Detection limits of RT-ddPCR, reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR), and reverse transcription nested PCR (RT-nested PCR) were determined using RNA extracted from metrologically validated SFTSV nucleic acid reference material. Then, diagnostic performance metrics of each PCR method were compared using RNA from 29 SFTS patients and 29 disease controls with scrub typhus. Statistical analyses of key laboratory parameters were performed to identify markers significantly correlated with SFTSV load, as defined by RNA copy number, in early SFTS patients. RT-ddPCR showed the lowest detection limit of 3.82 copies/μL among the three PCR methods. The sensitivity of RT-ddPCR was 82.75% in clinical samples, which was higher than that of RT-qPCR at 72.41%. The specificity of RT-ddPCR was 100% compared to 89.66% for RT-nested PCR. Overall, RT-ddPCR demonstrated the highest diagnostic performance among the three PCR methods, with an accuracy of 91.38% and an area under the curve value of 0.91. A strong correlation between viral RNA loads and laboratory parameters was observed in the early stage of SFTS, particularly with high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, lactate dehydrogenase, and activated partial thromboplastin time. Our findings demonstrate that a novel molecular diagnosis method using RT-ddPCR shows improved diagnostic performance for detecting SFTSV RNA from SFTS patients and potentially contributes to accurate early diagnosis and enhanced clinical diagnosis. IMPORTANCE Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is a high-mortality tick-borne infection caused by SFTS virus (SFTSV), and reliable molecular diagnosis is essential for patient care in endemic regions. Existing PCR-based assays for SFTS show limited sensitivity and specificity, particularly in patients with suspected or early-stage disease. Here, we describe the development and analytical validation of a reverse transcription droplet digital PCR (RT-ddPCR) assay for the detection and quantification of SFTSV RNA from patient sera. By using metrologically validated viral nucleic acid reference materials and clinical samples, this assay demonstrates significantly improved sensitivity and overall diagnostic performance compared with conventional reverse transcription quantitative PCR and reverse transcription nested PCR. RT-ddPCR can provide clinical microbiology laboratories with a useful tool to enhance early and reliable molecular diagnosis of SFTS.

This study aims to investigate whether reverse transcription droplet digital PCR (RT-ddPCR) provides improved diagnosis of SFTS compared to existing molecular diagnostic platforms. Detection limits of RT-ddPCR, reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR), and reverse transcription nested PCR (RT-nested PCR) were determined using RNA extracted from metrologically validated SFTSV nucleic acid reference material. Then, diagnostic performance metrics of each PCR method were compared using RNA from 29 SFTS patients and 29 disease controls with scrub typhus. Statistical analyses of key laboratory parameters were performed to identify markers significantly correlated with SFTSV load, as defined by RNA copy number, in early SFTS patients. RT-ddPCR showed the lowest detection limit of 3.82 copies/μL among the three PCR methods. The sensitivity of RT-ddPCR was 82.75% in clinical samples, which was higher than that of RT-qPCR at 72.41%. The specificity of RT-ddPCR was 100% compared to 89.66% for RT-nested PCR. Overall, RT-ddPCR demonstrated the highest diagnostic performance among the three PCR methods, with an accuracy of 91.38% and an area under the curve value of 0.91. A strong correlation between viral RNA loads and laboratory parameters was observed in the early stage of SFTS, particularly with high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, lactate dehydrogenase, and activated partial thromboplastin time. Our findings demonstrate that a novel molecular diagnosis method using RT-ddPCR shows improved diagnostic performance for detecting SFTSV RNA from SFTS patients and potentially contributes to accurate early diagnosis and enhanced clinical diagnosis.IMPORTANCESevere fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is a high-mortality tick-borne infection caused by SFTS virus (SFTSV), and reliable molecular diagnosis is essential for patient care in endemic regions. Existing PCR-based assays for SFTS show limited sensitivity and specificity, particularly in patients with suspected or early-stage disease. Here, we describe the development and analytical validation of a reverse transcription droplet digital PCR (RT-ddPCR) assay for the detection and quantification of SFTSV RNA from patient sera. By using metrologically validated viral nucleic acid reference materials and clinical samples, this assay demonstrates significantly improved sensitivity and overall diagnostic performance compared with conventional reverse transcription quantitative PCR and reverse transcription nested PCR. RT-ddPCR can provide clinical microbiology laboratories with a useful tool to enhance early and reliable molecular diagnosis of SFTS.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the diagnostic performance of reverse transcription droplet digital PCR (RT-ddPCR) for Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) compared to conventional RT-qPCR and RT-nested PCR. The research highlights the importance of early and accurate molecular diagnosis for SFTS, a tick-borne disease with high mortality and non-specific symptoms. The study demonstrates that RT-ddPCR has the lowest detection limit (3.82 copies/μL), higher sensitivity (82.75%) than RT-qPCR (72.41%), and 100% specificity compared to RT-nested PCR (89.66%). However, the evidence is limited to performance metrics and correlations, without addressing broader implications or causal relationships. The findings are significant for enhancing molecular diagnostic capabilities in endemic regions but require further validation for clinical implementation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 严重发热伴血小板减少综合征(发热伴血小板减少综合征)由发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(SFTSV)引起,其特点是高死亡率和非特异性临床表现,这使得早期准确的分子诊断至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究旨在调查与现有分子诊断平台相比,逆转录液滴数字 PCR (RT-ddPCR) 是否提供改进的 诊断 或 发热伴血小板减少综合征。
elements_zh.methods: RT-ddPCR、逆转录定量 PCR (RT-qPCR) 和逆转录巢式 PCR (RT-nested PCR) 的检测限是使用从经计量验证的 SFTSV 核酸参考材料中提取的 RNA 确定的。然后,使用 29 名 发热伴血小板减少综合征 患者和 29 名恙虫病对照者的 RNA 比较每种 PCR 方法的诊断性能指标。现有基于 PCR 的 发热伴血小板减少综合征 检测显示敏感性和特异性有限,特别是对于疑似或早期疾病的患者。
elements_zh.main_results: RT-ddPCR 在三种 PCR 方法中检测限最低,为 3.82 拷贝/μL。RT-ddPCR在临床样本中的敏感性为82.75%,高于RT-qPCR的72.41%。RT-ddPCR 的特异性为 100%,而 RT-巢式 PCR 的特异性为 89.66%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 我们的研究结果表明,使用 RT-ddPCR 的新型分子 诊断 方法在检测 发热伴血小板减少综合征 患者的 SFTSV RNA 方面显示出改进的诊断性能,并可能有助于准确的早期 诊断 和增强的临床 诊断。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: RT-ddPCR可以为临床微生物学实验室提供有用的工具来增强发热伴血小板减少综合征的早期和可靠的分子诊断。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 对关键实验室参数进行统计分析,以确定早期 发热伴血小板减少综合征 患者中与 SFTSV 负荷显着相关的标志物(根据 RNA 拷贝数定义)。在 发热伴血小板减少综合征 的早期阶段观察到病毒 RNA 载量与实验室参数之间存在很强的相关性,特别是与高敏 C 反应蛋白、天冬氨酸转氨酶、丙氨酸转氨酶、乳酸脱氢酶和活化部分凝血活酶时间。

papers.full_text: Abstract Background Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) incidence has risen steadily in China since the disease was first identified in 2009, with both case numbers and the geographic scope of reporting expanding over time. This study analyzed national surveillance data from 2010 to 2024 to characterize the evolving epidemiological patterns of SFTS. Methods This retrospective descriptive study included clinically diagnosed and laboratory-confirmed SFTS cases from China Information System for Disease Control and Prevention (CISDCP) (2010–2024). Joinpoint regression was used to analyze incidence trends. Case fatality rate (CFR) differences were assessed by chi-squared or Fisher’s exact tests, and the temporal trend was assessed by linear regression. Results During 2010–2024, a total of 30 provinces reported 34,055 cases. From 2010 to 2024, the incidence rate of SFTS in China showed a fluctuating upward trend, with an average annual percent change (AAPC) of 43.28% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 43.23%–43.33%;P < 0.01). Most cases were sporadic, with some regional clustering and rapid geographic expansion to previously unaffected areas. The number of reported cases in Anhui Province began to rise rapidly in 2022, making it the province with the highest number of reported cases in China in 2023 and 2024. The average CFR was 4.79%, and the CFR increased with age, reaching 9.15% among those aged 85 years and above. Conclusions During the period from 2010 to 2024, SFTS in China exhibited a marked increase in reported incidence and considerable geographical expansion. The disease is no longer confined to traditional high-risk areas; the rapid rise in cases in province such as Anhui suggests a critical need to re-evaluate the ecological and social factors driving its transmission. Although the overall population CFR showed a declining trend, mortality risk among elderly subgroups still needs attention. papers.title: Macrogenomic analysis showcases the diversity of tick RNA viruses in Mentougou, Beijing, China
papers.abstract: Background Ticks are the second most significant vector of human pathogens worldwide, with 911 documented species globally and a broad distributed across China. Currently, over 160 tick-borne viruses (TBVs) have been identified, several of which pose substantial threats to human health, such as Dabie bandavirus, Jingmen tick virus, Alongshan virus, Songling virus, Beiji nairovirus, and Langya henipavirus, raising increasing global attention. Despite their significance, the diversity of TBVs in Beijing remains poorly characterized. Methods In this study, we conducted metagenomic sequencing on tick samples collected from Mentougou District, Beijing. The obtained reads were subjected to quality control, de novo assembly, and viral sequence identification, followed by phylogenetic and evolutionary analyses. Results Our results identified 19 distinct viral species spanning 12 families, including Hepelivirales,Solemoviridae,Mymonaviridae,Nodaviridae,Permutotetraviridae,Phenuiviridae,Rhabdoviridae,Tombusviridae,Totiviridae,Peribunyaviridae,Flaviviridae,Nodaviridae,Tymoviridae,Tombusviridae . Among these, six novel viruses from five virus families were discovered. A potential pathogen, Tick jingmen-like virus, was also detected in the selected pathogens. These findings underscore the remarkable diversity of RNA viruses harbored by ticks in Mentougou District. Conclusions Our research findings reveal a previously unrecognized diversity of tick-borne viruses in the Mentougou District, Beijing, and provide essential baseline data for informing future surveillance strategies and guiding prevention and control of tick-borne diseases in the Beijing metropolitan area.

news.content: Published : July 29, 2026 - 11:00:00 As rising summer temperatures drive up tick activity, livestock farmers working in and around barns and pastures face heightened risk. Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, or SFTS, has no approved vaccine or treatment, making prevention — through proper work clothing and repellents — the only reliable defense. The Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency on Wednesday urged workers near livestock barns and pastures to wear long-sleeved clothing and boots, secure their cuffs and trouser hems, and apply tick repellents according to label instructions. South Korea is home to a variety of hard ticks, including the Asian longhorned tick, distributed across forests, grasslands and other outdoor environments. These ticks can transmit not only SFTS but also the pathogens behind Lyme disease, anaplasmosis and babesiosis. SFTS is a zoonotic disease transmitted through the bite of an infected tick. Both humans and livestock can develop symptoms including high fever, chills, muscle pain, vomiting and diarrhea, and severe cases can be fatal. According to the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency, 2,065 SFTS cases were reported in South Korea between 2013 and 2024, resulting in 381 deaths — a cumulative fatality rate of 18.5%. With no approved vaccine or treatment available, avoiding tick bites remains the most critical preventive measure. Livestock farms are particularly vulnerable because barns and grazing areas often border grasslands and brush where ticks thrive. Ticks in tall grass latch onto people and animals to feed, so workers in these areas should minimize exposed skin. Before heading out, workers should put on long-sleeved work clothes and boots and fasten cuffs and trouser hems tightly. Tick repellents should be applied at the recommended dosage and frequency. During work, sitting or lying directly on grass should be avoided, as should contact with wild animals. After finishing work, workers should carefully check their bodies and clothing for attached ticks. Grass around livestock barns should be cleared regularly, and livestock should also be inspected for ticks. Anyone who develops symptoms such as high fever, vomiting or diarrhea within two weeks of outdoor work should seek medical attention immediately and inform the doctor of any time spent working near barns or in grassy areas. Since 2023, the quarantine agency has been collecting and testing ticks at 76 sites near livestock farms across the country, monitoring the distribution of tick-borne pathogens year-round. No SFTS virus genetic material has been detected in ticks collected so far this year. However, the agency is stepping up regional surveillance as tick activity peaks during the summer months. The number of ticks testing positive for SFTS virus genes was 28 in 2023, 32 in 2024 and five last year. "We will continue to monitor hard ticks and tick-borne pathogens near livestock farms nationwide and promptly share information needed for prevention and disease control," agency chief Choe Jeong-rok said. "We also ask farmers and the general public to follow tick prevention guidelines during outdoor activities and work." This content was produced with the assistance of AI translation services.
